title: customer-polaris-incident-timeline-draft-samir-khan
content:
Purpose:
Draft notes / breadcrumbs for Customer Polaris outage (Feb 24-26) - internal timeline and short comms we can send to the account team + CSM. This is a scratchpad: commands tried, error snippets, hypotheses, and next steps.

Summary (short):
- Customer Polaris observed intermittent 5xx errors and request timeouts to their dedicated pool (dedicated-eu-west-2a) starting ~2026-02-24 08:42 UTC.
- Impact: ~30% of requests returned 502/503 or hung >30s; embeddings and generation both affected depending on routed model.
- Current status: mitigations applied (increased replica count, applied kernel fallback, rolling restart of affected nodes). Still monitoring; error rate dropped but not back to baseline as of 2026-02-27 04:00 UTC.

Timeline + actions (raw):
2026-02-24 08:42 UTC - First CSM alert (SUP-78910)
- Customer reports "requests intermittently failing with 502 and some responses truncated". Example id: req-Polaris-45321.
- Observed spike in 5xx on route: /v1/generate (model: redwood-large-v1-quant).

2026-02-24 09:10 UTC - Triage (me + Leah)
- Quick check: metrics show CPU on nodes in dedicated-eu-west-2a jumping to 95% and memory near full on 2/6 nodes.
- Error pattern: both generation and embeddings pipelines returning 502, but logs show different failure modes.

Commands run (initial):
- kubectl get pods -n dedicated-eu-west-2a  # confirm pod restarts and statuses
- kubectl top pods -n dedicated-eu-west-2a  # CPU/mem per pod
- docker stats $(docker ps -q --filter label=pool=dedicated-eu-west-2a) --no-stream
- curl -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-large-v1-quant","input":"hello"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" -v

Error snippets captured:
- log from pod inference-3:
  2026-02-24T09:24:12Z ERROR runtime: kubernetes node oom-kill invoked: container process killed (OOM)
- log from router:
  2026-02-24T09:26:01Z WARN request-id=req-Polaris-45321 downstream error: upstream returned 502 Bad Gateway (connection reset by peer)
- model server stacktrace (partial):
  panic: runtime error: index out of range [512] with length 512
  goroutine 153 [running]:
    github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/model.(*KVCache).Get(0xc0002f4000, 0xc0005a4000)
    	/home/runner/work/serving-runtime/model/kvcache.go:78 +0x1b4

2026-02-24 10:05 UTC - Quick mitigation
- Scaled dedicated pool from 6 -> 10 replicas (manual override of autoscaler) to absorb traffic.
- Applied kernel fallback on nodes running quantized models to use safer matmul path (less memory efficient but more stable).
- Notified Polaris that we are investigating (CSM coordinated initial message).

2026-02-24 13:00 UTC - Follow-up logs/observations
- After scale + fallback, error rate dropped to ~12% but not zero. Some pods still showing repeated OOMs.
- Observed that only pods serving the quantized variant redwood-large-v1-quant hit the OOMs; float32 variant redwood-large-v1 did not fail.

2026-02-25 02:40 UTC - Deep dive (Diego joined)
- Collected core dumps from crashed pods (dmesg shows oom-kill).
- Replayed failing requests locally against both variants. Reproduction: sending long-context requests (~3000 tokens) caused memory blowup on quantized runtime path.
- Commands used for repro:
  - python scripts/repro_request.py --model redwood-large-v1-quant --tokens 3000 --count 50
  - gdb -c core.1234 --batch -ex 'bt full'  (capture backtrace)

Error snippet from local repro run:
  runtime: out of memory: cannot allocate 134217728 bytes
  goroutine 200 [running]:
    github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/quant.(*Matmul).Execute(0xc0008a4000, 0xc0005b0000, 0x0)
    	/home/runner/work/serving-runtime/quant/matmul.go:210 +0x2f4

Hypotheses (current):
1) Quantized execution path has a regression in memory accounting for large-sequence KV-cache allocations - causes net allocation > available memory for some requests.
2) Kernel selection fallback should have prevented the crash, but only applied on some nodes; race in rollout caused mixed behavior.
3) Autoscaler did not add capacity early enough because pod readiness probe delays masked load and caused delayed scale-up.
4) There may be a request pattern from Polaris (long-context batch requests) exposing the bug more frequently than our internal benchmarks.

Temporary mitigations applied so far:
- Manually scaled pool to 10 replicas and pinned some traffic to float32 variant for heavy-context routes.
- Enabled safer matmul path on all quant nodes where possible.
- Raised alert thresholds to trigger earlier autoscaling.
- Blocked large-context (>=2500 tokens) on quant route via routing policy for Polaris (rate-limited, enforced at router layer).

Pending / Next steps (engineering):
- Priority: reproduce reliably and add unit test for KV cache boundary condition. (Diego)
- Run full memory sanitizer and fuzz tests on quant path. (Leah)
- Add guard in runtime to refuse allocations above threshold and return 429 instead of OOM. (Samir)
- Fix rollout so kernel fallback is an explicit config and applied consistently by release-engineering. (release-eng)
- Postmortem draft after root cause confirmed; include RCA and customer-impact timeline.

Draft internal comms (short) for account team / CSM:
Subject: Update on Polaris outage (Feb 24-26) - interim findings\nHi Jamie / CSM team,\nWanted to share an interim update on the incident affecting Polaris.\nWhat happened:\n- Between Feb 24-26 Polaris experienced intermittent 5xx/timeout errors on their dedicated pool. The root cause appears to be an issue in the quantized execution path where large-context requests sometimes cause runtime allocations that exceed available memory and trigger OOMs on some nodes.\nWhat we did:\n- Scaled the dedicated pool & applied a safer kernel fallback to reduce OOMs.\n- Routed large-context requests to float32 variant and rate-limited quantized route while we investigate.\n- Collected cores and logs; reproduction confirmed locally with long-context inputs.\nImpact:\n- Partial degradation (approx 10-30% of requests during peak) for 48 hours.\nNext steps:\n- Engineering to land a fix for memory accounting and add runtime guard to return 429 for requests that would exceed memory. ETA: 3 business days (target by 2026-03-02) - this is provisional.\n- Follow-up postmortem and customer-friendly RCA to be shared once root cause and fix are confirmed.\nApologies for the disruption - we know this impacted Polaris' workload and will prioritize preventing recurrence.\nBest,\nSamir (eng-sre)

Notes / things to remember for final RCA:
- Include exact request IDs with timestamps for customer (they asked for per-request visibility).
- Show graph of 5xx % by model variant (quant vs float32) during window.
- Explain rollout/fallback gap and autoscaler tuning changes.
- Offer credits / SLA remediation as per policy (coordinate with finance).

Open questions:
- Did Polaris recently change workload to more long-context calls? Need to ask CSM for traffic patterns.
- Are there other customers on dedicated-eu-west-2a using redwood-large-v1-quant with long contexts? (impact scope)
- Should we proactively disable quant route globally until fix lands? (risk vs cost tradeoff)

Scratch checklist (for me):
- [ ] Add unit test for KVCache bounds
- [ ] Run memory sanitizer on quant matmul path
- [ ] Implement allocation guard -> return 429
- [ ] PR for kernel-fallback rollout config (release-eng review)
- [ ] Draft customer-facing RCA (short + detailed appendix)

End of scratchpad.
